Mod written; reloading the page to check it.

ran trif check timsrobot.com/neon && trif reload && trif run 'const h=document.querySelector("main h1"); return {c:getComputedStyle(h).color, a:getComputedStyle(h).animationName}'; trif run 'await new Pr…

The title "Tim's Robot Internet Fixer" now glows like a hot-pink neon sign.

- **On page load:** the title starts out as dark, faint pink glass. After a moment it flickers on and off a few times over about 2½ seconds, then comes on for good and brightens to full glow.
- **After that:** the glow hums very slightly. The "o" in "Robot" acts like a faulty tube and sputters out for a split second every 7 seconds or so.
- **Reduced motion:** if your system is set to reduce motion, the title just glows steadily with no flicker.

I reloaded the page and checked it. The title starts unlit, finishes lit with the glow, and the mod reported no errors. I took a screenshot to confirm how it looks.
Now updating the title mod with the wave.
ran trif check timsrobot.com/neon && trif reload && trif run 'await new Promise(r=>setTimeout(r,3200)); const h=document.querySelector("main h1"); const chs=[...h.querySelectorA…
ran trif run 'return [...document.querySelectorAll("main h1 .nt-ch")].map(c=>Math.round(c.getBoundingClientRect().top)).join(" ")'; trif screenshot -o wave.png

I added the wave. Each letter of the title bobs up and down in turn, so a wave rolls across it from left to right. The neon flicker at load and the sputtering "o" in "Robot" still work. The title can still wrap between words if the page gets narrow, but never in the middle of a word. Screen readers still read it as the normal title.

**What I checked after reloading:** I measured the letter heights and saw the wave travelling across the title, and confirmed it in a screenshot. The mod reported no errors.

If your system is set to reduce motion, the wave is switched off.

The wave is part of the **Neon Title** mod, with the glow. To undo it, switch off **Neon Title** in the side panel, or ask me to.
